glosses: Participer à un brainstorming, une réunion de création d'idées.

examples.text: A La République en marche, pour brainstormer, on aime bien les Post-it et les gommettes. C’est graphique, c’est pratique : d’un coup d’œil, on peut voir si ça colle.

glosses: Obtenir comme résultat suite à un brainstorming.
To investigate something, or solve a problem using brainstorming.

examples.text: Meanwihle at Winterfell, another overdone scheme designed mainly to surprise the audience. In the black of her chambers, Sansa brainstorms with Littlefinger what Arya could want. “After she murders you, what does she become?” he asks. To which Sansa does everything but gasp and spit-take, widening her eyes and saying like she’s just realizing it for the first time, “Lady of Winterfell.”

On another occasion, when trying to brainstorm things I could do to make myself feel better despite all the pandemic restrictions, Woebot suggested I “try doing something nice for someone in your life,” like make a calming tea for my housemate or check in with a loved one.

glosses: To participate in a brainstorming session.
To think up (ideas); especially, to do so creatively.

examples.text: I need you to brainstorm some suggestions for next week's activity schedule.

glosses: A sudden thought, particularly one that solves a long-standing problem.

examples.text: I had been working on the problem for weeks, and then I had a brainstorm and saw that the solution was easy.

glosses: A session of brainstorming, investigating a problem to try to find solutions.

A terrible fielding error from Tony Graffanino proved costly. … Aaron Rowand collected an RBI double to get them off the mark before Graffanino's brainstorm. glosses: Alternative form of brain storm (“activity in the brain, such as a seizure or convulsion”).
